comment: The approved staging project, pinned in git.
WHY A HASH AND NOT THE REF: this file is committed, and a project ref is
part of a project-identifying URL. The guard only ever needs to answer
'is the connected project the approved one', which equality of hashes
settles without the ref appearing anywhere — not in this file, not in the
guard's output, not in a failure message.
WHY IT LIVES HERE AND NOT IN .env.staging: safeguard 3. Two values supplied
by the same environment file are one value. The environment supplies the
ref; git supplies the expectation; the sentinel row inside the database
supplies a third, independent assertion made by the database itself.
HOW TO FILL IT IN: see scripts/staging/README-steps.md, step 3. The command
projectRefSha256 is the lowercase hex SHA-256 of the project ref alone:
no scheme, no '.supabase.co', no trailing slash, no newline.
THE PLACEHOLDER IS DELIBERATELY HEX-SHAPED ('deadbeef' x 8) so that the
guard's not-placeholder check can be proven to fire. Until it is replaced,
approved-identity.test.mjs is red and names this file.
label: remotiv-staging
